title: Snapshot a volume and restore it in another zone
kills: "A snapshot can be restored only in the Availability Zone of its source volume."
cost: More than $0: two 2 GiB gp3 volumes and one snapshot, for the minutes that they exist. In the example of the Amazon EBS pricing page, gp3 storage costs $0.08 per GB-month, billed in per-second increments, with a 60-second minimum. The Amazon EBS User Guide names a standard snapshot rate of $0.05 per GB-month, and a snapshot charge is based on the size of the data being backed up: nothing was written to this volume.
cost_if_forgotten: More than $0 a day, every day until you delete them: 4 GiB of gp3 storage at $0.08 per GB-month, and the snapshot at $0.05 per GB-month of stored data.
read_only_alternative: These commands create nothing. List your own snapshots with their source volume, size and encryption: aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --query "Snapshots[].[SnapshotId,VolumeId,VolumeSize,Encrypted]" --output table Pick one snapshot ID as <SNAP_ID>, and list the volumes that were created from it, with their zones: aws ec2 describe-volumes --filters Name=snapshot-id,Values=<SNAP_ID> --query "Volumes[].[VolumeId,AvailabilityZone,Encrypted]" --output table If the lists are empty, answer the predict question of step 7 on paper.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Store the name of the first Availability Zone of this Region as AZ_A.
steps.expect: No output. AZ_A now holds a zone name, for example us-east-1a.

steps.text: Store the name of a second Availability Zone of the same Region as AZ_B.
steps.expect: No output. AZ_B now holds another zone name, for example us-east-1b. If AZ_B holds None, use a Region with two or more zones.

steps.text: Create an empty, encrypted 2 GiB gp3 volume in AZ_A, tagged for this book and this task. This is the source volume. From here, it is billed.
steps.expect: No output. VOL_ID now holds an ID that starts with vol-.

steps.text: Wait until the volume is available.
steps.expect: No output. The prompt comes back when the volume is available.

steps.text: Take a snapshot of the volume, with the same tags. The volume does not need to be attached to an instance.
steps.expect: No output. SNAP_ID now holds an ID that starts with snap-.

steps.text: Wait until the snapshot is completed. This can take a few minutes.
steps.expect: No output. The prompt comes back when the snapshot is completed.

steps.text: Create a volume from the snapshot in the other zone, AZ_B, with the same tags. Name gp3 as the type: in the CLI, gp2 is the default selection.
steps.expect: No output. NEW_ID now holds an ID that starts with vol-. AWS accepted a zone that differs from the zone of the source volume.
steps.predict: The snapshot comes from a volume in AZ_A. Can you create a volume from it in AZ_B?
steps.explain: Snapshot data is [replicated across all Availability Zones in the Region](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-restore-in-any-az-of-region), so you can [restore volumes in any Availability Zones](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-restore-in-any-az-of-region) of that Region. A volume and its instance [must be in the same Availability Zone](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-same-az-as-instance). To use the data in another zone, you take a snapshot and [create a duplicate volume in that zone](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-restore-volume-other-az). Until the snapshot blocks are [downloaded from Amazon S3 to the new volume](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-initialization-from-snapshot), a restored volume shows [increased I/O latency and decreased performance](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-initialization-from-snapshot).

steps.text: Read the zone, size, encryption and source snapshot of both volumes.
steps.expect: Two rows, in any order. The source volume shows the zone of AZ_A, 2, True and no snapshot ID. The new volume shows the zone of AZ_B, 2, True and SNAP_ID. You set no size and no encryption for the new volume: both came from the snapshot.

cleanup.text: Delete the restored volume. If AWS reports an error because the volume is still being created, wait one minute and run the command again.
Delete the snapshot. Deleting a snapshot has no effect on the volume.

verify.expect: An empty list. If an ID still shows, run the command again after one minute. Then check the snapshot too: aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --filters Name=tag:task,Values=ebs-t03 --query "Snapshots[].SnapshotId" must also return an empty list.

still_costs: The snapshot, until delete-snapshot has run. Find it with aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --filters Name=tag:task,Values=ebs-t03 --query "Snapshots[].SnapshotId" and delete it by its ID.

The two volumes, until delete-volume has run for each. If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, the variables are empty: find the volumes with the verify command and delete them by their IDs.

If a Recycle Bin retention rule for snapshots or volumes matches these resources, a deleted snapshot or volume stays in the Recycle Bin until the retention period ends, billed at the same rate as a regular one. List such rules with aws rbin list-rules --resource-type EBS_SNAPSHOT and again with --resource-type EBS_VOLUME
